title: Reading JSON Data with Pandas
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose of reading json data with pandas.
Choose Pandas APIs and parameters that match the input structure.
Apply the operations to deterministic Series and DataFrames.
Validate output shape, schema, data types and missing values.
Recognize edge cases and data-quality risks.

understand.concept: Pandas read_json loads records-oriented, column-oriented and line-delimited JSON into labeled data structures. Its orient and lines options must match the source layout. json_normalize flattens nested records. Inspect source shape and inferred dtypes after parsing.
understand.whyItMatters: Reliable data workflows ingest, combine, analyze and publish structured information. Correct parsing and transformations prevent silent data loss and misleading conclusions.
understand.analogy: A DataFrame workflow is like organizing labeled records: labels and matching rules determine how records are connected.
understand.summary: Pandas read_json loads records-oriented, column-oriented and line-delimited JSON into labeled data structures. Its orient and lines options must match the source layout. json_normalize flattens nested records. Inspect source shape and inferred dtypes after parsing.

explain.narrative: This lesson explores reading json data with pandas with small reproducible datasets. Inspect input structure before selecting parsing, join, time-frequency or export options. Validate resulting columns, row counts, index, dtypes and missing values. Pandas read_json loads records-oriented, column-oriented and line-delimited JSON into labeled data structures. Its orient and lines options must match the source layout. json_normalize flattens nested records. Inspect source shape and inferred dtypes after parsing.

examples.title: Records JSON
examples.code:
import pandas as pd
from io import StringIO
s=StringIO('[{"name":"Ari","score":8},{"name":"Bea","score":9}]')
df=pd.read_json(s)
print(df.score.tolist())
examples.explanation: This deterministic example demonstrates records json. Compare the output with the expected result and inspect the resulting data structure.

examples.title: Column JSON
examples.code:
import pandas as pd
from io import StringIO
s=StringIO('{"score":{"0":8,"1":9}}')
df=pd.read_json(s, orient='columns')
print(df.score.tolist())
examples.explanation: This deterministic example demonstrates column json. Compare the output with the expected result and inspect the resulting data structure.

examples.title: JSON lines
examples.code:
import pandas as pd
from io import StringIO
s=StringIO('{"id":1}\n{"id":2}')
df=pd.read_json(s, lines=True)
print(df.id.tolist())
examples.explanation: This deterministic example demonstrates json lines. Compare the output with the expected result and inspect the resulting data structure.

examples.title: Flatten nested records
examples.code:
import pandas as pd
rows=[{'id':1,'profile':{'city':'Kakinada'}},{'id':2,'profile':{'city':'Vizag'}}]
df=pd.json_normalize(rows)
print(df['profile.city'].tolist())
examples.explanation: This deterministic example demonstrates flatten nested records. Compare the output with the expected result and inspect the resulting data structure.

examples.title: Check required columns
examples.code:
import pandas as pd
from io import StringIO
s=StringIO('[{"id":1,"score":8}]')
df=pd.read_json(s)
print({'id','score'}.issubset(df.columns), len(df))
examples.explanation: This deterministic example demonstrates check required columns. Compare the output with the expected result and inspect the resulting data structure.
